en.html:
Kageaki"...Head of Records Management by name. In practice, chief of intelligence. And your superior... All this is Lieutenant Colonel Cannon?"
Kanae"Yes. In GHQ’s designs on Yamato, he is the one holding the actual power. It would hardly be an exaggeration to say so."
Kageaki"Then I was not simply hearing one lieutenant colonel’s views. It was GHQ’s own thinking being put before me...?"
Kanae"Truth and falsehood are a separate matter, of course. But you would do well to give his words that much weight."
Kageaki"...Truth and falsehood. Captain, about his request to me. Am I to accept it just as it stands?"
Kanae"Well... on that point. The plan is effective enough to leave one staring, I must say,"
Kanae"And a similar arrangement is being prepared for me as well. He may have further thoughts of his own. Even then, I doubt he is lying about wanting your cooperation."
Kageaki"...I see."

Kageaki"Captain. Have you agreed to this?"
Kanae"The arrangement for myself?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Kanae"I would not reject it out of hand."
Kageaki"...It hardly seems a proposal to suit your temperament."

Kanae"If accepting conquest by the League—by the British Commonwealth, in effect—is best for Yamato... then I follow that course and perform the part required of me."
Kanae"I have no objection. What I happen to like personally does not enter into it."
Kageaki"...Yes."

en.html:
Kanae"And you, Mr. Kageaki?"
Kageaki"...I have tried considering it."
Kageaki"This one point only: is the path Lieutenant Colonel Cannon offers really the best? Is that truly the best possibility we have?"
Kanae"Your conclusion?"
Kageaki"There will be peace for a time."
Kageaki"If the occupation forces drive Rokuhara out and take control of Yamato, we can expect improvements in many aspects of government... Unless the British Commonwealth chooses Yamato alone as the place to abandon its gentlemanship."
Kageaki"Yamato would acknowledge Britain as suzerain. Alongside Scandinavia, the three Baltic states and Mongolia, it would become another part of the wall containing the Russia. At last the Cage of Bears would be complete..."
Kageaki"Once that is done, are we expecting the Russian Empire simply to raise both hands?"
Kanae"..."
Kageaki"Their southward policy is their lifeline. I cannot see them quietly allowing it to be cut."
Kageaki"When they attempt to break that blockade by force... the first target will be—"
Kanae"—The newly occupied Yamato?"
Kageaki"Before the new rulers have established themselves, there is an opening. Someone will probably be thinking on those lines. In that case—Yamato’s spring does not last."
Kageaki"It will become a battleground for the Royal Knights and the Cossacks."
Kanae"Naturally, the British Commonwealth does not want such a thing either. They will try diplomacy. Concede some of Russia’s demands, perhaps, and ask for its entry into the League in exchange. Somewhere along those lines. ...But,"
Kanae"Matters need not be so obliging as to follow their plan."
Kageaki"No. As history has demonstrated..."
Kanae"Therefore you will refuse Lieutenant Colonel Cannon?"
Kageaki"...That is where it leaves me."

景明 「一時的な平和は訪れるでしょう」
景明 「進駐軍が六波羅を駆逐し、大和の統治権を 握ったなら、施政の多くの点で改善が期待で きます……大英連邦が大和に限って紳士道ジェントルマンシップを 放棄しない限りは」

景明 「しかしそうなった時、露帝は黙って両手を 上げるでしょうか？」
香奈枝 「……」
景明 「南下政策は彼らの生命線です。 　その切断をただ看過するとは思えません」

香奈枝 「――占領から間もない大和？」
景明 「支配体制が確立する前なら付け入る間隙は ある、おそらくそう考える者がいるでしょう。 　で、あれば――大和の春も長くは続かない」
景明 「女帝軍ロイヤルナイツと露帝軍コサックによる激戦の巷となります」
香奈枝 「もちろん、そんな事態ことは大英連邦も望みま せん。外交で決着をつけようとするでしょう。 　幾らかは露帝の要求にも応じ、代償に連盟 への参加を求める、その辺りで。……けれど」
香奈枝 「目論見通りにゆくとは限らない」
景明 「はい。 　過去の歴史が証明するように……」
香奈枝 「だからキャノン中佐の依頼は拒む――と？」
景明 「……そうなります」

Kageaki"Wise. To abandon the pride of an independent nation and live contentedly on the Queen charity—that is wisdom?"

Kageaki"For that one instant only, I felt I was seeing Lieutenant Colonel Cannon’s unguarded feelings... That is how it appeared to me."
Kanae"...Resentment of Queen’s Rule?"
Kageaki"I do not know. It really is speculation."
Kanae"————————"
Kanae"...Perhaps I ought to consider a response from our side after all...? No... It is too late now to set the Earl in motion..."
Kageaki"Captain?"
Kanae"Forgive me. It is nothing. Now... suppose your suspicion is correct. What happens then?"
Kageaki"If he should harbor rebellious intentions toward the Queen, then that would explain his eagerness to occupy Yamato. Establish himself in this country and turn his fangs against the British Commonwealth—"
Kageaki"Yamato would still become a battlefield. And in that case, affairs might be more confused, the people’s circumstances harsher, than in a war between the Commonwealth and Russia alone."
Kageaki"...To the point, perhaps, of making people long even for the Rokuhara days."
Kanae"“Longing for the old, muddy waters of Tanuma”? That is something I would ask to be spared."
Kageaki"I agree entirely."
Kanae"Then, as you see it, Mr. Kageaki, following my superior need not lead anywhere bright, whichever way matters turn. But—"
Kanae"Then do you have a prospect of your own, Mr. Kageaki? One that promises Yamato peace with greater certainty?"

en.html:
It was a searching question.

A path that would guarantee peace for Yamato.
Yes—if such a thing were easily found, no one would have suffered for it. Neither Prince Maidono nor my adoptive father.

Even those two, who must have possessed wider vision and deeper consideration, had been defeated by the growing confusion of the times. In the end they had lost their path and fallen.
That was how difficult it was to read a country’s future.

No experiment was required to establish that it exceeded Kageaki Minato’s ability.

And yet—

en.html:
Kageaki"I have no such prospect. Only one point I cannot let go."
Kanae"Cannot let go?"
Kageaki"Keeping Yamato at peace is difficult in the world as it stands. We cannot arrange to be free of military tension. But even if war must come eventually—"
Kageaki"I believe it ought to follow from the people of this country steering this country’s course. Captain Ootori."
Kanae"............"
Kageaki"If we are to be pushed about for another country’s convenience and arrive at war that way, it is too bitter. Besides, begin a war for another country’s convenience, and naturally its end is decided on the same basis."
Kageaki"After paying a terrible price, Yamato might have nothing to show for it... In the worst case, that is the history we could be left with. That much I find very difficult to accept."
Kageaki"Yamato’s rise and fall should at least be decided by Yamato’s will. That is the point I keep coming back to."
Kanae"............ ...Then..."
Kanae"For the sake of this point you cannot let go—Rokuhara’s army must not be destroyed just now."
Kanae"Is that right?"
Kageaki"...Yes."

Kageaki"When our talk reached strategy, Lieutenant Colonel Cannon said it himself: Rokuhara can be annihilated in a short time. But I am not seeing how."
Kageaki"Compare the forces on both sides. Rokuhara is hardly so overwhelmingly weak... Captain, is there really a plan that can do this?"
Kanae"There is."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"I have not got the details either. Information is very strictly controlled. Apart from the senior command, apparently only the units carrying it out have been informed."
Kanae"What I finally managed to discover was the date of the operation... and one weapon prepared for it."
Kageaki"...What weapon?"
Kanae"A Forged Bomb."
